mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening cycle, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls by > -0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% monthly for two months) and a rise in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.4% AND HOUST > +5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 0.1 percentage points for six consecutive months despite steady or rising GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates structural labor market slack, which does not translate into earnings pressure and is associated with neutral S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE changes in [-0.1, 0.1] pp for 6 consecutive months AND GDPC1 growth > 0%
regime_hint: structural labor slack with GDP growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are significantly negative or significantly positive during triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, with each 1% monthly increase in RSAFS associated with a 0.2% rise in 5-day returns.
failure_condition: The estimated coefficient on RSAFS growth is not statistically significant at 90% confidence in a rolling regression over any 12-month window.
